title: A Unified Electrostatic-to-Spin Framework for Asymmetric Multi-Gate CMOS Quantum Devices
authors: Zeheng Wang, Yan Liu, Yue Hao, Genquan Han
abstract: In advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) quantum chips, compact gate stacks make it difficult to connect lithographic geometry, electrostatic confinement and many-electron spin filling in one transparent model. This connection is central to design-technology co-optimization (DTCO). Here we develop a reduced-order analytical framework for asymmetric multigate silicon quantum-dot devices. Its electrostatic core, the Poisson-kernel coupled-interface Green-function (PK-GF) model, agrees with an independent finite-volume solution at the millivolt scale for the matched two-dimensional problem, without fitting to that solution. We then pass the gate-derived confinement, rather than a harmonic or fitted potential, to a spin-valley many-body calculation for a jellybean quantum dot with N = 2-17 electrons at B = 5 T. The unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) solution supports occupation-dependent, Wigner-molecule-like charge localization but likely overestimates spin polarization. Complete active-space configuration interaction (CASCI) supports a low-spin branch within the tested active spaces, which aligns with the experiments. The workflow therefore connects CMOS layout, device electrostatics, and potential-determined quantum observables, providing an auditable modelling layer for CMOS-based qubit design and DTCO.
summary: The paper presents an integrated theoretical framework connecting the electrostatics of complex CMOS quantum devices to their correlated electronic structure. By developing the accurate PK-GF model, the authors can calculate the confinement potential and then use advanced many-body techniques (UHF/CASCI) to predict spin filling and charge localization in silicon quantum dots. This establishes a vital tool for designing next-generation solid-state qubits.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a unified, end-to-end modeling framework that connects lithographic CMOS gate geometry electrostatics to the resulting many-electron spin and charge filling in quantum dots.
main_result: The authors successfully developed the Poisson-kernel coupled-interface Green-function (PK-GF) model, which accurately predicts device electrostatics at millivolt scales. Furthermore, they showed that the system operates in an interaction-dominated, Wigner-molecule-like regime, supporting low-spin ground states consistent with experiments.
method: The methodology combines advanced analytical electrostatics (PK-GF) to determine the confinement potential, which is then fed into correlated many-body quantum calculations using Unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) and Complete Active-Space Configuration Interaction (CASCI).
model_or_system: The system modeled is an asymmetric multi-gate silicon quantum dot fabricated within a CMOS architecture. The Hamiltonian incorporates Coulomb interactions, spin, and valley degrees of freedom, treating the gate potential as derived directly from device electrostatics.
key_observables: Spin density maps, charge localization (Wigner-molecule tendencies), ground state spin ($S=0$ support), addition energy spectrum, and the interaction-to-level-spacing ratio ($R$).
important_parameters: Electron number ($N = 2-17$), magnetic field ($B = 5 	ext{ T}$), and electrostatic potential derived from gate voltages.
main_assumptions: The PK-GF model assumes a specific coupling between interfaces, and while UHF is used for calculation, the authors note it may overestimate spin polarization compared to CASCI results. The convergence of the singlet-triplet gap is noted as potentially incomplete.
figures_summary: Figures compare the analytical PK-GF potential against independent Finite Volume (FV) solutions at millivolt scales; they also show charge density lobe profiles, pair correlation functions, and energy level comparisons between UHF and CASCI for different electron numbers.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the electrostatics by introducing and validating the PK-GF model against FV solvers. It then passes this derived potential into a spin-valley many-body calculation using UHF/CASCI to determine correlated electronic properties, culminating in an end-to-end workflow demonstration.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges solid-state device physics (CMOS lithography) directly into advanced quantum many-body theory, providing a crucial, auditable computational pipeline for designing qubits based on semiconductor platforms.
